title: Geometric subfamily of locally univalent functions, Blaschke products and quasidisk
summary: In this article, we consider the family $\mathcal{F}(α)$ defined for $α\in (0, 3]$ by \begin{align*} {\rm Re}\left(1+\frac{zf''(z)}{f'(z)}\right) > 1 - \fracα{2} \quad \text{for } z \in \mathbb{D}. \end{align*} Our primary objective is to show that this family possesses significant geometric and analytic properties, including connections with Blaschke products and the Schwarzian derivative, as well as its sharp bounds. Furthermore, we prove that if $f \in \mathcal{F}(α)$, then the image $f(\mathbb{D})$ is a quasidisk. We also show that if $f \in \mathcal{F}(α)$, then $\|S_f\| = 2α(2-α)$.…
